summary: A witness asks members to compare the proposed thickness with bags that suppliers can deliver.
realLife: Washington Senate report on SB 5323, 2019. Senate supporters raised the availability of different film thicknesses and sought a standard that suppliers could meet. Commerce and Ecology agreed with the researchers about dropping the scheduled increase to four mils. They opposed the researchers’ proposal to allow thin single-use bags for a charge.
inGame: needs: the committee is considering a minimum thickness and has supplier evidence.
gates: The committee is considering a minimum thickness and has supplier evidence.

turns.what: The supplier produces a firm delivery date.
turns.pulledBy: The supplier confirms stock meeting the proposed minimum.
turns.writesBack: The committee keeps its proposed specification.

turns.what: The committee considers extra time for orders already placed.
turns.pulledBy: The supplier can fill only a later order.
turns.writesBack: Members ask about a transition period.

turns.what: A legislator separates two changes that witnesses have been discussing together.
turns.pulledBy: The review team and agency agree about dropping a future increase but disagree about permitting the thinnest bags again.
turns.writesBack: The committee records support separately for each change.
